assets.section: A small corpus, chosen before the queries
assets.caption: All four methods search the same 32-page, 329-passage corpus. The frozen validation cohort has 12 queries in 12 dialogues. The corpus was selected first, eight pages per domain; queries require in-corpus gold evidence. Original holdout and explored dialogues are excluded. Results describe this restricted task.
assets.alt_text: Corpus hierarchy beside grouped bars for the training-design and held-out query counts in four domains.
assets.reading: We search 32 pages and 329 complete passages. The pilot uses 8 training queries and evaluation has 12 queries. Domain balance makes the design easy to inspect; it does not make twelve queries representative of all RAG workloads.

assets.section: A decision model versus an ordinary LLM
assets.caption: Conceptual A/B/C/D schematic. C and D use the same navigation controller with different scoring adapters; no performance values are implied.
assets.alt_text: Four horizontal paths compare lexical retrieval, lexical retrieval with Nimble, and hierarchical retrieval using either Nimble or Qwen.
assets.reading: A→B adds judging/rescoring; B→C changes discovery, candidate pools and workload; C→D replaces the model and scoring adapter under common navigation rules. The initial page corpus matches, but selected pages and downstream work can differ. These are end-to-end system comparisons, not causal isolation of architecture or training.

assets.caption: Frozen settings and the joint quality, latency, and validity requirements. These are criteria, not measured success.
assets.alt_text: Two-column table lists corpus, cohorts, controller limits, models, and the requirements for an efficiency claim.
assets.reading: This table is our contract with the experiment: corpus, cohort, models and resource limits are fixed. The mini study is explicitly exploratory. A successful run does not by itself establish a retrieval-quality or efficiency win.

The error bars are exploratory dialogue-bootstrap intervals, not proof of a universal ordering. Exact normalized-text R@1 is A: 33.33%; B: 58.33%; C: 50.00%; D: 50.00%; this sensitivity leaves strict-ID scoring primary and does not establish equivalence or an efficiency win.

assets.section: Does the decision model earn its place?
assets.caption: Run evaluation-20261030T222218Z; mini_3h: 12 validation queries / 12 dialogues / 32 pages; attempted/scheduled: A 12/12, B 12/12, C 12/12, D 12/12; status complete. C minus D R@1 in percentage points versus zero (exploratory comparison), and ratio of median full-query times versus one. Intervals are 95% percentile bounds from 10,000 paired whole-dialogue resamples within domain. Verdict: exploratory mini comparison. Validity gates must also pass. Restricted-corpus mini comparison is exploratory and cannot confirm the original full-study claim.
assets.alt_text: Two interval plots compare the quality difference with zero and the time ratio with equality.
assets.reading: C−D Recall@1 is 0.0 percentage points, with a 95% interval from -33.3 to 33.3. The median-time ratio C/D is 1.87 (95% interval 1.80–2.07); a ratio above one means Nimble took longer. Equal observed recall is not evidence of equivalence. The interval resamples queries from one captured run, not repeated runs or hardware. Different selected branches and workloads are included in this end-to-end time comparison.

assets.reading: The recorded verdict is **exploratory mini comparison**. Completion of all four mini methods is distinct from running our original local 259-query study. Input fit, warm residency and timing integrity describe execution validity; they do not turn an uncertain quality comparison into a win.

assets.section: Where did the hierarchy lose the answer?
assets.caption: Run evaluation-20261030T222218Z; mini_3h: 12 validation queries / 12 dialogues / 32 pages; attempted/scheduled: A 12/12, B 12/12, C 12/12, D 12/12; status complete. Strict structural-ID counts partition every scheduled query into a rank-one ID hit, retained-page ID miss, pruned gold page, execution failure, or unattempted. The categories sum to the scheduled denominator. An ID miss may still match the target text; see the exact-text sensitivity. Restricted-corpus mini comparison is exploratory and cannot confirm the original full-study claim.
assets.alt_text: Two stacked bars show Nimble and Qwen strict-ID hits, retained-page ID misses, page pruning, and execution status.
assets.reading:
Nimble pruned the gold page on 0 queries; Qwen did so on 2. Retaining a page is only the first hurdle: Nimble then had 7 rank-one structural-ID misses on retained pages, and Qwen 5. An ID miss may still match the target text.

**Score resolution:** C made 275 scored request groups and D 235. Excluding singletons, D had all-equal scores in 177/234 groups and some tie in 231/234; C had 0/273 all-equal groups and 0/273 groups with any tie. Equal scores fall back to candidate-ID order. These are dependent request groups, not extra evaluation queries; ties can be appropriate for irrelevant candidates. They describe this adapter, not a general ordinary-LLM limitation or a cause of its speed.

assets.alt_text: Domain rows compare the four methods’ recall at rank one with explicit query counts.
assets.reading: The domain breakdown is an inspection aid, not four small leaderboards. With three validation queries per domain, a single changed answer moves recall by 33.3 percentage points. Do not choose a domain-specific winner from these counts.
